newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says monetary policy aims at basis of recovery.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says monetary policy aims at basis of recovery.

text.p: Japan's monetary policy aims to ensure a basis for economic recovery while keeping watch over economic conditions, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday.
"Our monetary policy will continue to put emphasis on making the basis for economic recovery firmer while keeping watch over economic developments," Matsushita said.
He said the BOJ would make decisions on monetary policy not just by looking at individual factors such as currencies and stock prices but at overall economic movements.
He said an effect could be seen from the rise in the consumption tax, in which private consumption had now retreated after a rush in demand before the rise.
"Basically, the gradual recovery trend is continuing," Matsushita said.
This view had been backed up by reports given by BOJ branch managers at their two-day meeting in Tokyo, which ends on Tuesday, he said.
But Japan still needs to determine whether its economic recovery can overcome the effects of the rise in the consumption tax on April 1, he said.

Falls in prices had generally come to a halt, partly due to the weakness of the yen. He said he did not see upward pressures on domestic prices increasing, although the central bank would need to keep careful watch over their movements.
Matsushita also said the BOJ would like to keep watch over how the domestic economy would react to movements in currencies and interest rates, and deal with such reactions as appropriate.
